title: U.G. Krishnamurti passes away
description: The Hindu, Today's Paper / National. Death notice-obituary reporting the death at Vallecrosia, Italy on 22 March 2007; names survivors (two daughters, a son). URL carried by reader comments on spiritualteachers.org and the cuke.com compilation; page itself not opened.

title: Philosopher U.G. Krishnamurti passes away
description: Oneindia (agency-style report). Died 2.30 pm 22 March 2007 at a friend's villa in 'Vallecorsia' (sic) after seven weeks bedridden following a fall; cremated the next day by film-maker Mahesh Bhatt without rituals.

title: DNA (Daily News & Analysis) death notice, as reproduced on cuke.com
description: David Chadwick's cuke.com Death & Dying page compiles the DNA notice (age given as 89) and notes that The Hindu reported the death on 25 March 2007. Original DNA URL not recovered.

title: Obituary of U.G. Krishnamurti by Mukunda Rao (official site)
description: Mukunda Rao's obituary account on the official site: fall seven weeks before death, death 2.30 pm 22 March 2007 in the apartment built for him by friends Lucia, Anita and Giovanni at Vallecrosia; cremation by Mahesh Bhatt at 2.45 pm the next day, no rites.

title: Remembering UG Krishnamurti (WELL memorial page)
description: J.C. Thomas's memorial on the WELL archive; gives age 89 and recalls the first book compiled by Rodney Arms (1982). One memorial line gives 25 March as date of death (conflict with 22 March).

title: U.G. Krishnamurti died (prembuddha, Dutch site)
description: Dutch personal site notice of the death; the only Dutch-language-sphere item found.

title: U.G. Krishnamurti R.I.P. (Thomas Ligotti Online thread)
description: Reader-forum death thread, March 2007; the forum also has a U.G. Krishnamurti subforum (forumdisplay.php?f=42).

title: The death of UG (Scribd compilation)
description: Scribd document compiling accounts of the death and cremation at Vallecrosia.

title: The negating guru: U.G. Krishnamurti (spiritualteachers.org profile)
description: Profile; its comment thread cites The Hindu March 2007 report and names survivors Usha, Bharati and Kumar.

title: Indian and Western newspaper obituaries not yet located (Deccan Herald, Times of India, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Telegraph Kolkata, Outlook, Frontline, India Today, Tehelka, Guardian, Times, Daily Telegraph, Independent, NY Times, LA Times, Riviera/Sanremo press)
description: Target list from the research brief. Wave 2 and wave 5 searches surfaced no URL for any of these; the only confirmed mainstream Indian items are The Hindu (25 Mar 2007), Oneindia (24 Mar 2007) and the DNA notice quoted on cuke.com. Recorded as a lead for follow-up. Wave 5 ran six targeted obituary searches (Indian dailies, UK/US broadsheets, Outlook/Frontline/India Today/Tehelka, rediff/ToI/DNA, Ligurian papers in Italian): still no hit. Mainstream 2007 record remains The Hindu, Oneindia, DNA (via cuke).

title: Resources & Archive: press clippings about U.G., 1970–2000 (index)
description: Official site index of lifetime press clippings: Deccan Herald 1981–93 pieces on the 'Natural State', money and the 'godman' label; Sunday Observer 1982 review ('an honest, muddled, minor voice'); City magazine (Bombay) 1987; and others. Individual clippings not opened.

title: Deccan Herald pieces on U.G. Krishnamurti (5 Feb 1990; 12 Sep 1993)
description: Deccan Herald (Bangalore) clippings reproduced on the official press-articles page: 5 Feb 1990 profile of UG as down-to-earth despite his 'Godman' reputation, noting that money matters to him; 12 Sep 1993 piece. Earlier 1981–89 DH items are implied by the index but not individually dated in search snippets.

title: Sunday Observer items on U.G. (4 Jul 1982 review; 7 Jan 1990; 14–20 Mar 1993)
description: Sunday Observer (Bombay) clippings on the official press page: 4 Jul 1982 review calling UG 'an honest, muddled, minor voice, for whom we must be thankful' (The Mystique of Enlightenment); 7 Jan 1990 item carrying a Khushwant Singh quote; 14–20 Mar 1993 piece on UG and self-discovery.

title: Bombay City Magazine feature on U.G. (1987)
description: 1987 City Magazine (Bombay) interview-feature quoting Mahesh Bhatt and referring to Chandra Shekhar; UG's line 'The hows dished out in the market-place are not for me. The one who is living doesn't ask how to live' is reprinted from it on fan sites. Listed on the official press page.

title: Illustrated Weekly of India, 25 May 1986 — Mahesh Bhatt on U.G. ('He is my friend, philosopher and guide'); known in the catalogue as 'Two Seers'
description: Illustrated Weekly item dated 25 May 1986 on the official press page, quoting Bhatt 'He is my friend, philosopher and guide' and UG on selfishness and God (WELL ntbook3). Wave-4 chronology calls it 'Two Seers' (UG's attack on JK after JK's death); that title did not surface in search snippets and remains unconfirmed.

title: The Patriot (New Delhi) interview with U.G., 1989
description: Listed on the WELL archive index as 'Delhi 1989 Patriot'; the brief attributes it to Khushwant Singh (unverified). Related: the Remembering UG talks index lists two audio recordings 'Kushwant Singh in India, 1989', and the Travels with UG blog (post dated Dec 2005/06) describes an afternoon interview with Khushwant Singh in New Delhi — so Singh interviewed UG at least twice; no Singh column text found.

title: What the Press and Others Say About U.G. (WELL, ntbook3.htm)
description: WELL archive page compiling press quotations and reactions to UG (from The Natural State book apparatus).

title: The Mountain Path, June 1995 — review of Larry Morris's poems on U.G. (The Natural Man: Poems on U.G.)
description: Ramanasramam journal The Mountain Path, June 1995: 'a delightful collection of so-called poems (epiphanies would be a better description)' about Morris's relationship with UG, 'an iconoclast extraordinaire and unabashed scoundrel'. Listed on the official 'books about UG' page; the Jayanthi 1995 issue PDF is on realization.org. The snippet does not name the title, so the match to The Natural Man is probable, not certain.

title: U.G. Krishnamurti: The Divine Anarchist (Mariana Caplan)
description: Mariana Caplan's 2002 profile essay, reprinted on advaita.org.uk and Awakening Times.

title: A Taste of Life: The Last Days of U.G. Krishnamurti (review, Journal of Cancer Research and Therapeutics)
description: Medical-journal book review of Mahesh Bhatt's account of UG's dying.

title: UG in a comic book: the strange life of the other Krishnamurti who broke away from Jiddu
description: Scroll.in feature/excerpt on the graphic novel This Dog Barking (HarperCollins India, 2017), reproducing panels.

title: The bit about Parveen Babi that you won't find in the UG Krishnamurti biography
description: Scroll.in Reel piece publishing the Parveen Babi outtake panels from This Dog Barking; covers Bhatt bringing Babi to UG (1979–80).

title: Drawing out UG Krishnamurti (book review)
description: The Tribune (Chandigarh) review of the graphic novel This Dog Barking.

title: Mahesh Bhatt to UG Krishnamurti: I was in a spiritual coma. Why did you wake me up?
description: ThePrint PageTurner excerpt (28 Apr 2026) from The Ashes Are Warm: Memories of a Lifetime Spent with UG Krishnamurti (Rupa, Apr 2026; diaries compiled by Sunita Pant Bansal); recounts an early confrontation at UG's house.

title: Mahesh Bhatt shoots for a documentary based on eminent thinker UG Krishnamurti's life
description: NDTV-syndicated entertainment news item on Bhatt filming for a UG documentary (presumably the project that became The Natural State; Bhatt was interviewed in Varanasi). Date not captured.

title: यूजी कृष्णमूर्ति – अद्वितीय भारतीय विद्रोही दार्शनिक (birth-anniversary special)
description: Outlook Hindi birth-anniversary (9 July) feature on UG as a unique Indian rebel philosopher. The only Outlook-group item found.

title: Who is UG Krishnamurti (Suresh N., Medium)
description: Medium essay with photographs.

title: My Journey with UG Krishnamurti (Uma Balaji, on sureshn13 Medium)
description: Memoir essay describing the Poornakutee balcony and the peepul tree by the Anjaneya temple, Bangalore.

title: On UG Krishnamurti (adesa, Medium)
description: Medium reflection essay.

title: U.G. Krishnamurti's Swan Song [Updated] (alysion42, Medium)
description: Reproduces 'My Swan Song' (dictated Feb 2007) in a wording that differs from the WELL copy, with inserted commentary.

title: Understanding U.G. Krishnamurti: an interview with Mark Whitwell, parts 1, 2 and 4
description: Multi-part Medium interview series with yoga teacher Mark Whitwell on his years with UG (2000–07); part 1 describes a suitcase of photographs.

title: My Life with U.G. Krishnamurti (Mark Whitwell, Medium)
description: Whitwell's memoir essay with photographs.

title: U.G.'s referents: The Mystique of Enlightenment (professordeino, Substack)
description: Substack close-reading essay on The Mystique of Enlightenment.

title: The Anti-Guru: U.G. Krishnamurti and the End of Seeking (The Observing I, Substack)
description: Substack post/podcast episode on UG as anti-guru.

title: Buddha at the Gas Pump #177: Louis Brawley (Substack page)
description: Rick Archer's Substack page for the BatGap interview with Louis Brawley (author of Goner) about UG's last years.

title: The Natural Man blog (Larry Morris)
description: Larry Morris's blog republishing The Natural Man material and the Mountain Path review.

title: Long-form and magazine items not located (Open, Caravan, Mint Lounge, The India Forum 2021, Swarajya, Firstpost, LiveMint, Tricycle, What Is Enlightenment?/EnlightenNext, Parabola, Nonduality, Noumenon, Yoga Journal, Hinduism Today, Spirituality & Health, Quest, Sufi journals; Khushwant Singh / Pritish Nandy print interviews; Mahesh Bhatt columns in HT, Mumbai Mirror, Mid-Day, Firstpost, Quint, Wire)
description: Targets from the brief for which no URL has yet surfaced in waves 2–5. Note: Gulf News 'Goodbye my love' (Bhatt on Parveen Babi, 18 Sept 2006) is not about UG and should not be catalogued as such. Wave 5 searches confirmed negatives: Tricycle's Krishnamurti pieces ('The Shadow Side of Krishnamurti') are about Jiddu; The India Forum's 2021 Krishnamurti essay/letters (T.M. Krishna) are about Jiddu; no Noumenon/Connection/Tattva Viveka article, only Noumenon-Verlag book listings; no Dutch press (only the fan site onderzoekhetzelf.nl).

title: 'The Natural State': Jane Campion and Matt Dougherty on their Telluride documentary (interview)
description: Deadline interview with executive producer Jane Campion and director Matt Dougherty ahead of the Telluride world premiere (preview implies Saturday 5 Sept; Tribune gives 7 Sept).

title: The Natural State review: decoding India's fiercest anti-guru U.G. Krishnamurti
description: Variety India review of the 100-minute documentary.

title: Mahesh Bhatt on Matthew Dougherty's The Natural State: 'The film has been born, the director has been born, UG Krishnamurti has escaped'
description: Variety India interview with co-executive producer Mahesh Bhatt; film 'nearly 17 years in the making'.

title: 'UG threw me back into life': Mahesh Bhatt on the brutal, beautiful mystery of UG Krishnamurti
description: The Tribune interview with Bhatt around the Telluride premiere (gives premiere date 7 Sept 2026).

title: The Natural State – Telluride FF 2026 review by Diane Carson
description: Alliance of Women Film Journalists review ('a decidedly unusual documentary'); Carson's Telluride overview part two also covers it.

title: Woodstock Review: The Natural State examines the contradictory state of non-belief
description: The Film Stage review from Woodstock Film Festival 2026: 'a challenging text, in no small part because U.G. himself is challenging'.

title: A film 18 years in the making found its footing in a Hudson Valley WhatsApp group
description: Local feature on the making of The Natural State (begun 2008 from Julie Thayer's 1989 footage); Woodstock FF screening 17 Oct 2026, Orpheum Theatre, Saugerties.

title: A Conversation with Matthew Dougherty (The Natural State) — Hammer to Nail
description: Hammer to Nail interview with the director on digitising Thayer's 'hundreds of hours' of lo-fi home video.

title: The Natural State (2026) – Woodstock 2026 (Unseen Films)
description: Unseen Films festival review from Woodstock 2026.

title: The Natural State (Next Best Picture)
description: Next Best Picture Telluride review, 5 Sep 2026: 7/10, 'engrossing but unsatisfying'; notes Dougherty builds scepticism into editing and score.

title: The Natural State – Upstate Films programme page
description: Woodstock FF / Upstate Films listing (99 min); TV Guide lists 1h42.

title: The UG Krishnamurti Documentary (Center for Independent Documentary project page)
description: Fiscal-sponsor project page under the working title, describing the film as built from Thayer's late-1980s footage.

title: 2026 film coverage not located (Variety US, IndieWire, Hollywood Reporter, Screen Daily, The Hindu, Scroll, Telluride and Woodstock printed programmes)
description: Three wave-5 searches on these outlets returned nothing; Variety India is the only Variety property to have reviewed the film. Deadline's Telluride review roundup lists an entry 'Director Matt Dougherty, E.P. Jane Campion Explore Riveting Anti-Guru U.G. Krishnamurti in The Natural State', but only the interview URL surfaced.

title: U.G. Krishnamurti ci ha lasciato (riflessioni.it forum)
description: Italian spirituality-forum thread announcing the death (gives 14:30 as time of death). Only Italian-language 2007 item found; no Secolo XIX / La Stampa / Riviera press hit.

title: L'anarchismo religioso di UG Krishnamurti
description: A – Rivista Anarchica no. 337 (2008): essay on UG as a religious anarchist, opening with his death 'in una villa di Vallecrosia, poco più di un anno fa'; cites his critique of the 'spiritual market'.

title: Illustrated Weekly of India, 31 Mar–6 Apr 1985 — 'Tempestuous association' (Mahesh Bhatt on the 'raging guru')
description: Bhatt recalls his tempestuous association with UG, 'the raging guru'. On the official press page.

title: Illustrated Weekly of India, 11 Dec 1988 — 'The how is absent for me'
description: Interview/feature quoted in the WELL press compilation; not visible in the ugkrishnamurti.in snippet.

title: Illustrated Weekly of India, 29 Dec 1990 — 'Cosmic Naxalite'
description: Feature headed 'Cosmic Naxalite', listed on the official press page.

title: Illustrated Weekly of India, 12–18 Dec 1992 — 'Man has to be saved from God' / 'Offers no hope' (review of Bhatt's U.G. Krishnamurti: A Life)
description: Review of the Viking 1992 biography, with a companion Bhatt piece; the official press page's reviewer found the biography disappointing.

title: Udayavani and Cine Blitz clippings on U.G. (official press page)
description: The official press-articles section also lists Kannada daily Udayavani and film magazine Cine Blitz among 1970s–90s clippings; dates not shown in snippets.

title: The Mountain Path, January 1991 — review of a book on U.G.
description: Listed on the official 'books about UG' page; title of the book reviewed not shown in snippet (candidates: Mind is a Myth 1988 or Mystique reprint).

title: NON-FICTION: The anti-guru's last days (review of A Taste of Life)
description: Dawn (Pakistan) Books & Authors review: 'an unputdownable book'; notes UG's refusal of treatment and Bhatt's repetitive phrasing. Date c. 2009–10 (age metadata).

title: The Tribune Saturday Extra, 20 June 2009 — on Mahesh Bhatt's A Taste of Life
description: Magazine-section review: 'somewhat repetitive' but 'compelling reading'; 'UG did not want to be God; Mahesh Bhatt has made him out as one'. Byline not visible.

title: Book Review: This Dog Barking — The Strange Story of UG Krishnamurti
description: DNA review by Gargi Gupta of the Harper Element graphic biography; notes few in India know UG, who rejected Hinduism's tenets and discouraged followers.

title: Book Review: Spiritual thought becomes grist for new graphic novel
description: The Sunday Guardian review of This Dog Barking, on text, artwork and the authors' ideas about the graphic-novel form (Wagner, Tibetan Buddhism).

title: Enlightenment is Physical: An Introduction to U.G. Krishnamurti
description: Reality Sandwich essay by Mukunda Rao, excerpted from The Biology of Enlightenment (HarperCollins India 2010).

title: The Influence of UG Krishnamurti on Yoga / An Introduction to UG Krishnamurti (Heart of Yoga blog)
description: Mark Whitwell's Heart of Yoga blog posts on UG (12 Mar 2021 and an undated introduction).

title: Inside the heartbreaking love story of Mahesh Bhatt and Parveen Babi
description: Masala.com feature: when Babi's doctor proposed ECT after her 1979 breakdown, Bhatt instead took her to 'his philosopher friend, U.G. Krishnamurti'. Representative of Parveen Babi coverage that mentions UG.

title: Der trügerische Schein der Erleuchtung — review (Mystica.tv) and Jetzt-TV profile
description: German web review of the Noumenon-Verlag 2011 translation (trans. Daniel Herbst), noting UG is often confused with Jiddu; Jetzt-TV 'Gelebte Weisheit' profile page. No German print-magazine article found.

title: UG Krishnamurti — Onderzoek Het Zelf (Dutch reference site)
description: Dutch-language profile page on UG's views on truth, the anti-guru role and negation. Fan reference site, not press; the only Dutch item found besides the prembuddha death notice.

title: Mahesh Bhatt on 'anti-guru' UG Krishnamurti as his guru (review of The Ashes Are Warm)
description: The Tribune book review by Harjinder Singh: the book 'is more about Bhatt than UG', narration self-righteous, women underdeveloped; 366 pp., Rs 495.

title: 'UG Krishnamurti ended satsang to find me whisky': Mahesh Bhatt recalls unusual guru moment
description: PTI story in The Tribune around the book launch: a 1980s Bengaluru episode in which UG ended a satsang early because Bhatt craved whisky.

title: Book Review: Mahesh Bhatt's 'The Ashes Are Warm' is a deeply personal exploration of truth and presence
description: Free Press Journal review: 'less a memoir than an intimate chronicle of survival'; praises restrained writing.

title: Book Review: 'The Ashes Are Warm' by Mahesh Bhatt (Storizen)
description: Storizen review (also in Storizen Magazine, 21 Jun 2026 via PressReader): UG as a disruptive force rather than a spiritual guide; Bhatt's turmoil in the 1970s–80s and grief after 2007.

title: Hindustan Times Books page review of The Ashes Are Warm (Nawaid Anjum)
description: Review by Nawaid Anjum in the Hindustan Times Books page, announced in his X post of c. 29 June 2026; HT URL not recovered (truncated link).

title: Mahesh Bhatt on his mother Shrin: 'The woman who belonged everywhere' (excerpt from The Ashes Are Warm)
description: Scroll.in Reel excerpt, with permission from Rupa; includes Bhatt's account of first meeting UG ('a figure standing at the top of a staircase').

title: The Natural State (review, Hammer to Nail)
description: Hammer to Nail Telluride review: 'a gripping exploration of spiritual longing, psychological vulnerability and the danger of surrendering oneself to another person's authority'; premise of Julie Thayer going to the Alps 'to have her ego destroyed'.

title: A pointer toward The Natural State (2026) — Telluride 2026 (Unseen Films)
description: Unseen Films Telluride preview note, preceding its October Woodstock review.

title: Telluride Film Festival 2026: read all of Deadline's reviews (roundup entry on The Natural State)
description: Deadline's Telluride roundup (Yahoo syndication) lists 'Director Matt Dougherty, E.P. Jane Campion Explore Riveting Anti-Guru U.G. Krishnamurti In The Natural State'; the deadline.com review URL itself was not surfaced.

title: The Natural State — Rotten Tomatoes and official film site
description: Aggregator page and the official site thenaturalstate.film (synopsis, festival dates).
